jobs.description: TheProvost’s Postdoctoral Fellowship Programat the University of Notre Dame supports outstanding early-career scholars in science, engineering, and the liberal arts who seek to make a difference in the world.For the 2027-2029 academic years, the College of Arts and Letters will appoint a cohort of eight postdoctoral fellows in residence at the University. The following units will host one fellow each:Department of Art, Art History, and Design;Department of English;Department of German, Slavic, and Eurasian Studies;Department of Philosophy;Department of Romance Languages and Literatures;Department of Theology;Initiative on Race and Resilience; and theProgram in History and Philosophy of Science. For more information about each unit and potential areas of study within them, see theProgram’s webpage.TheProgram in History and Philosophy of Scienceat theReilly Center for Science, Technology, and Valuesin the College of Arts and Letters at the University of Notre Dame invites applications for a postdoctoral fellowship in the history of modern science or the integrated history and philosophy of modern science.Applicants should have completed a PhD in the history of science or the philosophy of science, or be near completion. We especially welcome applications from scholars of the modern physical sciences (notably physics, chemistry, earth sciences, and astronomy), and projects with transnational or global scope. Research in harmony with initiatives supported by the University’sStrategic Frameworkis also welcomed.  The selected fellow will have significant support and time to pursue independent research, writing, and scholarly networking, with the goal of generating significant progress toward a scholarly monograph. The successful applicant will also benefit from interactions with our program’s notable strength in the philosophy of modern physics, as well as our larger community of historians and philosophers of science and medicine. Teaching is not required, but there will be opportunities for teaching at the undergraduate and graduate levels in the STS undergraduate minor and the HPS graduate program. The fellow will also participate in the intellectual life of the program, including attending our weekly colloquium talks in the first half of each semester, and the annual conference in the spring semester. This fellowship also offers faculty mentorship from senior historians of science and philosophers of science, dedicated office space, institutional IT support and library access.These prestigious fellowships target exceptional early-career scholars interested in advancing their careers in an academic environment that is both committed to disciplinary expertise and vibrant in interdisciplinary exchange. The College will appoint the fellows for a two-year term. They will receive an annual salary of $75,000 and an additional $15,000 to cover expenses related to research endeavors and further training. Hosting units will provide fellows with office space and work together with the Director of Postdoctoral Studies in the College to identify primary faculty mentors for the fellows’ proposed research projects. Co-mentors with appointments at the University can be named at the discretion of the director and hosting units. Every six months, the director and hosting units will review the fellows’ progress in their research and discuss future plans.Monetary support and faculty mentoring will be coupled with professional development and networking opportunities in and outside of the hosting unit. The Provost’s Fellows will be a part of a university-wide cohort of distinguished researchers who participate regularly in lectures, colloquia, and panel discussions designed to advance their research and career aspirations.Notre Dame has recently launchedeight strategic initiativesintended to identify research areas where the University can make a significant impact. These initiatives will support dramatically expanded research efforts in the arts; data, AI, and computing; democracy; ethics; health and well-being; sustainability, and global Catholicism. The University also sustains premier research programs in traditional disciplines as well as having more than 30 university-wide interdisciplinary centers and institutes. Candidates for the Provost’s Fellowship are encouraged to explore these opportunities, as well as the areas of excellence and growth identified by hosting units, and to select a field of study in which they can excel.Eligibility:Applicants must have successfully completed (or plan to complete) a doctoral degree between June 2024 and June 2027. Earlier dates may be accepted if maternity or paternity leave, or Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) leave occurred within the past two years. Scholars of all nationalities may apply. We welcome candidates with or without permanent full-time research or teaching positions. Doctoral candidates and graduates of the University of Notre Dame, as well as current postdoctoral scholars at the University, are not eligible.ApplicationApplicants should submit the following via theInterfolio website:A cover letter including your research trajectory, your motivations for applying, and the fellowship’s role in furthering your career goals.  Your cover letter should not exceed 4 pages in length, double-spaced, with font size 12 and 1-inch margins.Your curriculum vitae.A statement describing your previous research accomplishments and your proposed research project(s) for the fellowship period. This statement may include the names of faculty from whom you would like to receive mentorship if you should be selected as a fellow, and why you think you would benefit from their expertise and experience. Please do not, however, reach out to faculty in the hosting department or institute to arrange a primary mentor or co-mentor prior to submitting your application. Your research statement should not exceed 5 pages in length, double-spaced, with font size 12 and 1-inch margins.Candidates must submit a writing sample representative of their own work (no more than 10,000 words in length).Candidates must also arrange for at least three letters of recommendation to be submitted via Interfolio by the deadline. Please do not ask your letter writers to email their letters directly. Applications without the full complement of letters will not be reviewed.Timeline:The application deadline is December 1, 2026, at 11:59 pm EST. Decision by March 1, 2027.Frequently Asked Questions can be found on the Program’s webpage.For further questions or concerns about the application process, please email[email protected].Timeline:The application deadline is December 1, 2026, at 11:59 pm EST. jobs.description: Position DescriptionChapman University invites applications for two tenure-track positions at the rank of Assistant Professor in Philosophy, beginning August 1, 2027.  The appointments will be in the Smith Institute for Political Economy and Philosophy and the Philosophy Department within Schmid College of Science and Technology.Successful candidates are expected to conduct independent and original research at the highest academic level, provide excellent teaching, and demonstrate academic leadership. Since the positions are jointly appointed in the Smith Institute, we seek candidates interested in working together with people from different disciplinary backgrounds. In particular, candidates should demonstrate an interest in putting their lines of philosophical inquiry into conversation with insights from economics or the other social sciences and humanities.While broadly speaking both positions will be focused on questions in political and social philosophy, the committee is especially interested in people with one of two backgrounds. First, we are looking for candidates who approach issues germane to the Smith Institute’s mission through a PPE-methodology. Second, we are interested in candidates who approach these questions in a historical context. The committee will employ a broad understanding of both PPE and historical approaches.The mission of the Smith Institute is to reintegrate the study of the humanities and economics in the spirit of Adam Smith, the author ofThe Theory of Moral SentimentsandAn Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations, and to recombine research and undergraduate education as a discovery process in the spirit of Vernon Smith, a founder of experimental economics.Chapman University is a nationally ranked, R2 Carnegie Classified, private institution offering traditional undergraduate and graduate programs in the heart of Orange County, one of Southern California’s most diverse and vibrant regions. Chapman’s campuses are home to nearly 10,000 students representing 50 states, three territories, and 87 countries. The 11 schools and colleges of Chapman offer 65 bachelors, 53 masters, and six doctoral programs, along with nearly 60 minors and 17 accelerated and bridge programs. Classes are taught by the more than 1,100 dedicated faculty members who are leaders in their fields, including Nobel Prize recipients, MacArthur Fellows, National Medal of Science honorees, former U.S. Supreme Court clerks, and Emmy, Grammy, and Academy Award winners.QualificationsOf particular interest will be candidates specialized in one or more of the following: Political Philosophy, PPE (Philosophy, Politics and Economics), and the History of Political and Economic Thought.Required:PhD in Philosophy or its equivalent from an accredited institution.Strong potential for impactful scholarly contributions in the field of Philosophy, or a closely related field.Commitment to teaching and mentoring.A strong desire to work in an interdisciplinary environment.Preferred:Prior teaching experience in undergraduate Philosophy (or closely related field) and PPE courses.Application Instructions:Interested and qualified candidates should submit:Cover LetterCVResearch StatementTeaching StatementWriting SampleThree Confidential Letters of RecommendationFor inquiries, please email: Samantha Aronson[email protected]Successful completion of a background check is required for each final candidate. The salary range for the positions is $80,000 - $100,000 a year.  Salary is competitive and will be commensurate with experience. Positions are contingent on final budget approval.Equal Employment Opportunity StatementChapman University is an equal opportunity employer that provides equal employment opportunities to all individuals, regardless of their protected characteristics.  All qualified applicants and employees are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, military and veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by state or federal law.

jobs.description: The Program of Liberal Studies (PLS) seeks to hire a tenure-track assistant professor in Philosophy beginning August 2027. Duties will include research, teaching and service. The area of research specialization is the text-based approach to History of Philosophy, with a preference for the Pre-Modern or Early Modern periods.We are especially interested in applications from candidates with a broad liberal arts background. Teaching responsibility will be a 2-2 course load, including the Program's Great Books seminars and its three philosophy courses (tutorials): Philosophical Inquiry, Ethics, and Metaphysics and Epistemology (see our website,http://pls.nd.edu, for course descriptions). The candidate may also contribute to other disciplinary-based courses in the department as appropriate and will advise undergraduate senior theses.PLS is a multidisciplinary, liberal arts department with roughly 125 undergraduate majors. Founded in 1950, it has its own tenure-line faculty drawn from different disciplines and committed to an integrated program of studies grounded in the reading of core primary texts. PLS students move through a seminar sequence from the ancients to the contemporary world and also take subject-specific classes in literature, philosophy, theology, fine arts, intellectual and cultural history, political theory, and the natural and social sciences. All PLS faculty teach seminars, as well as courses in their respective disciplines.

new_jobs.description: About the roleThe post is offered on a one-year fixed term contract, full-time basis, with a start date of January 2027. Main purpose of the job: The successful candidate will be expected primarily to provide teaching, supervision, and administrative duties associated with the following modules: ‘Philosophy of Space and Time’, ‘Formal Epistemology’, and ‘Science and Pseudoscience’. Duties will also include supervision of dissertations. The appointee will also supervise BA and MA dissertations and act as a personal tutor for some students. The appointee may also be required to carry out other specific tasks and duties, commensurate with the spirit of the role, as requested by the Head of Department. Application materials: Applicants will need to submit: (i) a CV; (ii) one writing sample, totalling no more than 12,000 words; (iii) a cover letter, of no more than two sides (A4); and (iv) two reference letters. For the reference letters, applicants will need to arrange for two referees to submit letters of reference prior to the deadline. These should be sent to[email protected]About youCandidates must hold a PhD in Philosophy or be soon to be awarded one. Applicants must demonstrate expertise in the areas to be taught, with an aptitude for teaching and be committed to fostering a positive learning environment for students.About usThe Department of Philosophy at UCL is one of the leading philosophy departments in the UK. new_jobs.description: The Department of Philosophy at San José State University is pleased to announce a search for a full-time assistant professor (tenure-track) position in Philosophy of Technology beginning in August 2027. While the department welcomes candidates whose research and teaching engage deeply with questions about emerging technologies, the department is open to a broad construal of the technology that is the focus of the candidate’s philosophical work.The College of Humanities & the Arts, and the University more broadly, actively pursues the theme of the intersection of the humanities and the arts with technology. Given our location in Silicon Valley and our commitment to supporting the development of ethical technologies through our newAdvanced Institute for Ethical Technologies, there are significant interdisciplinary collaborative opportunities for a faculty member exploring these issues through a philosophical lens. The Institute, in the process of being formed, pursues the need for human-centered technology that values privacy and ethical decision-making.  In partnership with the Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Library and the San Jose Public Library, the College has also established theDigital Humanities Centeras a site of curriculum development, faculty research, student engagement, and public-facing programming and events.The Department of Philosophy (https://www.sjsu.edu/philosophy/) is one of ten departments and schools in the College of Humanities & the Arts (https://www.sjsu.edu/humanitiesandarts/departments.php) and offers Philosophy BA and MA programs. We value and engage with a plurality of philosophical traditions and styles, as well as the perspectives of our diverse community of faculty and students. We are committed to creating learning environments, a departmental culture, and a larger philosophical community that welcomes all who want to explore philosophy.The Department of Philosophy and San José State University value institutional excellence and are committed to advancing equity through research, teaching, and service. We enroll more than 40,000 students, many of whom are historically underserved; approximately 45% of our undergraduate students are first-generation college students and 38% are Pell Grant recipients. In addition, we are both a Hispanic Serving Institution (HSI) and an Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander Serving Institution (AANAPISI). SJSU aspires to create holistic learning environments that facilitate both individual and collective transformation. We seek teacher-scholars who cultivate inclusive, empowering spaces for mutual learning, skill-building, and knowledge exchange for all students. Our commitment to lifelong learning supports meaningful connections among faculty, staff, students, alumni, and the broader communities we serve.We invite all applicants to include a Statement of Institutional Excellence (or incorporate it into your cover letter) to share how your lived and professional experiences will contribute to the SJSU community—particularly in relation to student success. A guide to writing this statement can be found atSJSU Institutional Excellence Statement Guidelines.Required QualificationsPh.D. in Philosophy prior to appointmentA demonstrated record of effective teachingEvidence of the ability to publish and engage in professional activities in the area of philosophy of technologyApplicants should demonstrate an awareness of and sensitivity to the educational goals of a socially and economically diverse student population as might have been gained in cross-cultural study, training, teaching, and other comparable experiencePreferred QualificationsPriority will be given to candidates who possess one or more of the following attributes:Demonstrated expertise in an additional area of philosophy (such as global philosophy, ethics, epistemology, political philosophy, philosophy of disability, etc.) that informs their philosophical engagement with technologyInterests in pursuing cross-tradition engagement in doing philosophical work on technologyCapacity to contribute to interdisciplinary research and teaching through the Advanced Institute for Ethical Technology (https://www.sjsu.edu/ha-in-action/engage/ai-et.php)Teaching interests and competencies that could contribute to the department’s teaching needs in history of philosophy, ethical theory, phenomenology, Africana philosophy, Asian philosophy, applied ethics (e.g., professional and business ethics, environmental ethics, medical ethics), or phenomenologyCapacity to supervise MA students interested in pursuing ourAdvanced Certificate in Ethics of Science and Emerging Technologies.Key ResponsibilitiesIn addition to teaching courses in the area of specialization, including “Science, Technology, and Human Values” and “Computers, Ethics and Society”, the candidate will be expected to teach other general education courses that could include Introduction to Philosophy; Logic and Critical Reasoning; Moral Issues; Asian Philosophy; and Professional and Business Ethics; or courses in the history of philosophy.  The candidate will also contribute to the department’s ability to offer courses throughSJSU Online.The candidate will sustain an ongoing record of research, scholarship, and/or creative activities, as well as other professional engagement.The candidate will participate in shared governance, usually in department, college, and university committees and other service assignments.Faculty shall organize all their classes within the Canvas Learning Management System (LMS).The candidate must demonstrate awareness and experience in understanding the needs of a student population of great diversity – in age, abilities, cultural background, ethnicity, religion, economic background, primary language, sexual orientation, gender identity, and academic preparation – through inclusive course materials, teaching strategies, and advisement.Other DutiesNote that all San José State University employees are considered mandated reporters under the California Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act and are required to comply with the requirements set forth in CSU Executive Order 1083 as a condition of employment. Pursuant to the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy and Campus Crime Statistics Act (Clery Act) and CSU systemwide policy, some faculty duties may lead to designation as a Campus Security Authority (CSA). CSAs are required to complete Clery Act training and to immediately report Clery incidents to the institution.Faculty employees must complete CSU employee training as assigned and required based on their role (e.g., Data Security, FERPA, Preventing Discrimination and Harassment, Title IX, Health and Safety). The President may recommend or require compliance with safety measures that decrease the likelihood of COVID-19 transmission or illness and allows the core mission and activities of the campus to continue.

new_jobs.description: Position DescriptionJohns Hopkins University’sSchool of Government and Policyseeks to recruit multiple tenured and tenure-track faculty in multiple disciplines and fields of study, including (but not limited to) political science, law, sociology, history, philosophy, computer science, and economics.While searching broadly, we have a particular interest in faculty conducting research on the following topics of inquiry:Cities and Communities:State and local policymaking and implementation. Applications are encouraged from candidates in civil engineering, economics, history, law, sociology, political science, public administration, or urban planning, with research interests including local governance, state capacity, urban innovation, housing and real estate, public education and school choice, transportation and land use, or local finance and budgeting.Frontier AI:The implications of highly advanced AI for government and society. Applications are encouraged from candidates from a wide range of disciplines including computer science, economics, philosophy, law, political science cognitive science, and sociology. Research interests might include: AI alignment and governance; the government, societal, and labor market impacts of and adaptation to AI; the use of AI to simulate and design policy interventions; regulatory theory and innovation; institutional design and innovation; and AI evaluation, auditing and verification.Political Philosophy and Theory:Ambitious, foundational, big-picture political philosophy and/or political theory with direct relevance to government and policy, advancing the school's mission of shoring up and renewing the core institutions of liberal democracy. Applications are encouraged from candidates who are problem-focused and syncretistic, drawing on different conceptual, methodological, and empirical approaches and orienting themselves outward from philosophy/theory toward the world, with particular interest in candidates whose work intersects with or complements other parts of the School's research strengths.Public-Sector Innovation and Management:How governments and other public-sector organizations function, why they succeed or fail, and how to change them to more effectively solve public problems. Applications are encouraged from candidates in the social sciences, management, history, organizational behavior, psychology, urban planning, operations research, industrial and systems engineering, management science, public management, or public policy. Research interests might include: institutional reform and organizational change; public innovation and problem solving; public-sector management, budgeting, procurement, contracting, and operations; state capacity and bureaucratic performance; organizational structure, behavior, learning, and culture; the adoption and management of technology in government, including the organizational challenges of effective implementation and how technologies affect public-sector organizations, policy, and governance.Regulation, Bureaucracy, and Public Administration:Why governments so often fail to deliver what policies promise, and what institutional redesigns would enable them to do so. Applications are encouraged from candidates in political science, law, public administration, history, sociology, or other fields whose work is changing the terms of academic and public debate. Research interests might include: the politics of civil service and personnel systems; federalism and the implementation of large public programs; intergovernmental relations; regulation, enforcement, and capture; administrative procedure and policy analysis; or state capacity more broadly.Across all these searches, we seek candidates who can work and learn across disciplines and take seriously the need to improve government effectiveness. We welcome candidates who have worked within public-sector and policymaking institutions and alongside government reformers from across the political spectrum. We are also interested in candidates who wish to investigate the challenges and opportunities of governing and deploying artificial intelligence.About the School of Government and PolicyAnchored at the Hopkins Bloomberg Center in the heart of Washington, D.C., the School of Government and Policy will be a hub of discovery, collaboration, and impact. new_jobs.description: Position Title: Endowed Bartlett Chair Professor/Associate Professor, Free EnterpriseReq ID: R0006517Time Type: Full timeLocation: Waltham, MADescription:Job Description SummaryBentley University invites applications for the Bartlett Chair of Free Enterprise, an endowed position at the Associate or Full Professor level, to begin in Fall 2027.Funded by a generous gift from Bruce and Patricia Bartlett, the Bartlett Chair of Free Enterprise affirms Bentley's commitment to fostering free expression, intellectual pluralism, and the constructive exchange of ideas as central to a liberal education. new_jobs.description: The American Philosophical Association invites applications for the position of editor(s)-in-chief of theJournal of the American Philosophical Association(J-APA), its flagship research journal.Launched in 2015 in cooperation with Cambridge University Press, J‑APA is now a leading international journal publishing scholarship in all topics, areas, styles, and traditions of philosophy. An editor-in-chief or co-editors-in-chief will be appointed in spring 2027, in time for a transition period beginning no later than July 2027. Policies are set by a governing committee made up of the editor(s)-in-chief and representatives of CUP, the editorial team, and the APA’s Board of Officers. new_jobs.description: About the roleThe full-time postdoctoral fellow in philosophy will conduct independent and collaborative research in the Philosophical Moral Psychology Lab under the supervision of Dr Joanna Demaree-Cotton. The post is fixed term for 3 years. The fellow will work as part of a collaborative interdisciplinary team contributing to projects within the Philosophical Moral Psychology Lab. Though they may work on various topics in the lab, the fellow’s research will include contributions to the Moral Psychology of Autonomy in Healthcare project, looking at topics such as: autonomy-based rights in healthcare; inequities in respect for medical autonomy; what it means to be ‘listened to’; whether there are moral duties of listening; cross-cultural understandings of medical autonomy and patient consent.   The lab includes researchers with complementary skills in philosophical and psychological methods respectively. The fellow will be expected to collaborate with researchers whose expertise lies in experimental moral psychology.   The fellow will be expected to actively contribute to research relevant to the Philosophical Moral Psychology Lab, and also provide guidance to junior members of the research group including research assistants, PhD students, and/or project volunteers.  The Philosophical Moral Psychology Lab conducts interdisciplinary research that draws on moral philosophy, ethics, experimental philosophy and moral psychology. The lab investigates the factors and psychological processes that shape moral intuitions, moral reasoning, and moral agency, and develops empirically-informed contributions to normative debates in philosophical ethics. Current research areas include: consent and autonomy; gender bias and medical ethics; moral dilemmas; moral responsibility and blame; moral duties to the dead; animal and AI ethics. For more information about the research group, see https://moralpsychlab.web.ox.ac.uk/home.   The start date of the role is 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter, and no later than 1 October 2027.About youYou will hold a PhD or DPhil in Philosophy (or related field), or be close to completion by the advertised closing date for this application.   It is essential for the postholder to have expertise in ethics and moral philosophy. The possession of interdisciplinary skills is desirable, and interest in relevant interdisciplinary research (e.g. psychologically-informed ethics, philosophically-informed moral psychology, experimental philosophy, and/or philosophy of psychology) is essential. The successful candidate will have demonstrated excellent research skills and willingness to work collaboratively with others.   The duties and skills required are described in further detail in the job description, which can be found at the above link.
